result.title: AgenticFinBench: Benchmarking Financial Agents on Diverse Tasks from Real-World Requests
result.summary: Financial agents are becoming an important class of real-world AI systems. Financial tasks vary widely in type and difficulty, and many are open-ended with no ground-truth answers. However, existing benchmarks neither capture this breadth and open-endedness nor separate grounding from correctness. To bridge this gap, we introduce $\textbf{AgenticFinBench}$, a benchmark of 230 real-world financial tasks spanning 8 categories, 2 languages, and 4 complexity levels. We also propose a reference-free evaluation framework that combines question-specific rubrics with a two-stage claim audit that detects hallucinations, defined as claims absent from the agent's trace and refuted by external evidence. This framework better matches how financial work is assessed in practice. Experiments across 18 agent configurations reveal three key findings: (1) Ignoring hallucinations can overstate agent performance: hallucination auditing lowers the baseline leader's score by 7.58 points and moves it to fourth place. (2) Harness differences explain more variation in evidence grounding than model differences (28.6% vs 8.8%). (3) Quality scores fall from 89.44 on direct retrieval to 79.18 on the most complex tasks. Case studies show that agents struggle to explain how events affect company profits or stock prices, compare financial data on a consistent basis, and justify their conclusions. By releasing AgenticFinBench, we aim to advance financial reasoning, factual verification, and agent design for more reliable responses to diverse real-world financial requests. Our project page is at $\textbf{https://nashnovaresearch.github.io/AgenticFinBench/}$.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 AgenticFinBench，包含 230 个真实金融请求任务（8 类、2 语言、4 难度），并给出无参考答案的评估框架：用题级 rubric 加两阶段 claim 审计检测「轨迹中无依据且被外部证据否定」的幻觉，评测了 18 种 agent 配置。
AI.relevance_reason: 金融 agent 任务本身不涉及视觉 latent，但其区分「证据落地」与「答案正确性」并依轨迹审计无依据主张的做法，可能可供核查用于评估 LVR 中答案是否真正使用视觉证据；另「harness 差异大于模型差异」的发现或可类比推理脚手架的作用。
